paragraphs: This paper studies transformer reasoning by asking which logical statements can describe a classifier’s behavior. The numerical precision used during computation matters for this question. The authors show that, in the finite-precision setting they analyze, a single attention head can attend to only a constant number of tokens and cannot express uniform attention over an arbitrarily growing context.

They therefore examine a more expressive setting in which computation uses precision that grows logarithmically with context length. This lets the analysis address transformers capable of attending across the whole input. The main result translates any such transformer classifier into a first-order logical sentence extended with majority-vote quantifiers, alongside the usual universal and existential quantifiers.

The contribution gives a logical upper bound on what these classifiers can express. It connects a concrete computational resource—numerical precision—to a formal description of reasoning power. The authors identify this as the tightest known upper bound and the first logical characterization for log-precision transformers.
neurips-2023-a-logic-for-expressing-log-.tldr: The paper expresses log-precision transformer classifiers in first-order logic with majority quantifiers, connecting numerical precision to reasoning power.

paragraphs: Differentially private stochastic gradient descent has a costly internal step: computing a separate gradient norm for every example in a batch. These norms support gradient clipping, so their computational cost becomes an important bottleneck when batches are large. Existing acceleration methods exploit decompositions associated with intermediate linear operations in the loss computation.

The paper develops a common framework that extends this decomposition approach to arbitrary intermediate operations, including nonlinear ones. This broadens the mathematical tools available for computing per-example norms efficiently. The framework also provides components that can improve existing decompositions for familiar operations, specifically fully connected layers and embedding computations.

For those operations, the authors derive improvements in both runtime and storage requirements. Preliminary numerical experiments show substantial effects from these improvements. The contribution therefore combines a broader framework with concrete efficiency gains in selected cases; the abstract does not claim that every nonlinear operation receives the same acceleration. Its practical significance is reducing the computational burden of a central DP-SGD step.
neurips-2023-a-unified-fast-gradient-cli.tldr: A generalized gradient-decomposition framework accelerates per-example norm calculations for DP-SGD, with runtime and storage improvements for selected layers.

paragraphs: Training or fine-tuning neural networks directly on small devices is constrained by available memory. The paper examines forward gradient descent as a potential alternative to memory-intensive backpropagation. However, forward gradient descent has its own obstacle: dependencies between layers can prevent computations from running in parallel and leave hardware resources underused.

The proposed AsyncFGD framework reduces these dependencies through asynchronous execution. Different modules can use stale parameter values rather than waiting for every parameter to be fully current. This makes it possible to overlap more computation across modules, addressing the resource-utilization problem that otherwise weakens the appeal of forward gradient training.

The authors provide a theoretical analysis showing convergence to critical points, which does not by itself establish convergence to globally optimal solutions. Experiments on NVIDIA’s AGX Orin embedded device report lower memory consumption and improved hardware efficiency. Together, these results support asynchronous forward gradient training as a practical direction for learning under device memory constraints.
neurips-2023-accelerated-on-device-forwa.tldr: AsyncFGD uses asynchronous module updates to make forward gradient training more memory-efficient and better utilize embedded hardware.

paragraphs: Some adversarial classification problems are asymmetric: an attacker wants a dangerous item to be labeled harmless. The paper formalizes robustness certification for a binary classifier with one sensitive class. This focuses the guarantee on preventing false negatives for that class, matching the direction of attacks described in the abstract.

The proposed feature-convex network combines a Lipschitz-continuous feature map with an input-convex neural network. For the sensitive class, the authors derive deterministic, closed-form robustness radii for arbitrary lp norms. These radii give an efficiently computable measure of how much an input can change while remaining protected by the certificate. Additional theory examines decision-region geometry and approximation capabilities.

The authors also establish a lower bound on the probability of perfectly fitting unstructured uniform data in sufficiently high dimensions. Experiments on malware classification and subsets of three image datasets report substantial certified radii under l1, l2, and linfinity measures, with much greater computational efficiency than competitive baselines. These findings support the architecture for the asymmetric setting studied.
neurips-2023-asymmetric-certified-robust.tldr: Feature-convex networks provide efficiently computable robustness certificates for a sensitive class in asymmetric binary classification.

paragraphs: Reward design is difficult because frequent feedback can encourage behavior that differs from the intended objective. A designer’s heuristic may help an agent learn, but it can also reward an unhelpful shortcut. The authors investigate settings where even potential-based reward shaping significantly harms performance, motivating a more adaptive way to incorporate auxiliary feedback.

Their framework learns behavior alignment reward functions through a bi-level objective. These functions combine the environment’s primary rewards with auxiliary rewards representing heuristics and domain knowledge. Rather than fixing that combination beforehand, the method learns how to blend the signals. The framework can also adapt policy optimization to mitigate shortcomings associated with limitations and biases of the underlying reinforcement learning algorithm.

Evaluations range from small experiments to high-dimensional control tasks and include both helpful and harmful auxiliary rewards. The reported results show consistently strong solutions even with misaligned or poorly specified heuristics. This supports treating reward combination as an optimization problem, making designer knowledge useful without assuming that every supplied heuristic is beneficial.
neurips-2023-behavior-alignment-via-rewa.tldr: A bi-level optimization framework learns how to combine primary and heuristic rewards, improving resilience to poorly specified auxiliary feedback.

paragraphs: CMExam provides a structured benchmark for evaluating Chinese medical question answering. It contains more than 60,000 multiple-choice questions drawn from the Chinese National Medical Licensing Examination. Alongside answer selection, solution explanations support open-ended evaluation of the reasoning models generate, giving the benchmark two complementary forms of assessment.

Medical professionals added annotations for disease groups, clinical departments, medical disciplines, competency areas, and question difficulty. These labels allow analyses beyond a single overall score, organizing questions by their medical content and demands. The authors describe CMExam as, to their knowledge, the first Chinese medical examination dataset with comprehensive medical annotations.

Among the evaluated systems, GPT-4 achieved the best accuracy at 61.6%, with a weighted F1 score of 0.617, while the reported human accuracy was 71.6%. Models generated relevant explanations and improved after fine-tuning, but their explanations remained below the desired standard. The findings identify gaps in both answer accuracy and explanation quality within this examination setting.
neurips-2023-benchmarking-large-language.tldr: CMExam benchmarks Chinese medical answers and explanations, revealing a substantial accuracy gap between the best evaluated model and humans.

paragraphs: This paper asks whether being able to learn a distribution from clean data also implies being able to learn it when an adversary contaminates the data. Its central finding is that the answer depends on the adversary’s allowed operation. Adding contamination and removing information lead to different theoretical relationships between ordinary learning and robust learning.

For additive contamination, the authors show that learnability implies robust learnability. The implication also covers Huber contamination. But it does not hold in general when the adversary can perform subtractive contamination. Thus, the positive result for added contamination cannot simply be carried over to a setting where an adversary can remove parts of the evidence.

This distinction also separates realizable from agnostic distribution learning: success when the target belongs to the assumed class does not imply success in the more general agnostic setting. The authors contrast this with other learning settings, including PAC learning of function classes. They additionally examine related implications for compression schemes and differentially private learnability.
neurips-2023-distribution-learnability-a.tldr: Distribution learnability implies robustness to additive contamination, but this implication fails in general for subtractive contamination.

paragraphs: Adapting a large pretrained vision model often involves adding lightweight adapters so that relatively few parameters need updating. This paper asks whether adaptation parameters can also be reused across layers. That changes the design question from how small each adapter should be to how much of its structure different layers can share.

Adapter Re-Composing, or ARC, constructs bottleneck operations using symmetric down-projections and up-projections. These operations are shared across layers. The method then learns low-dimensional rescaling coefficients to produce adapters suited to individual layers. Shared structure therefore provides a common foundation, while the coefficients allow adaptation to vary with layer position.

The authors evaluate ARC on 24 downstream image classification tasks using several Vision Transformer variants. They report compelling transfer performance with fewer new parameters, supporting parameter reuse as a way to reduce adaptation cost while maintaining satisfactory results. The contribution is a concrete sharing strategy that preserves layer-specific adjustment without requiring every layer to carry an entirely separate set of adaptation parameters.
neurips-2023-efficient-adaptation-of-lar.tldr: ARC shares adapter projections across Vision Transformer layers and learns small rescaling coefficients to reduce adaptation parameters.

paragraphs: Training an energy-based generative model with cross-entropy requires a gradient that depends on samples from the model’s own distribution. Obtaining representative samples can be difficult when the sampling process mixes slowly. The paper addresses this obstacle using a relationship from nonequilibrium thermodynamics together with sequential Monte Carlo tools.

The method modifies the unadjusted Langevin algorithm by attaching a weight to each sampling walker. These weights enable estimation of the cross-entropy gradient at any step of gradient descent. The construction draws on the Jarzynski equality to bypass sampling biases associated with slow mixing, avoiding the uncontrolled approximations used by standard contrastive divergence.

Numerical experiments cover Gaussian mixture distributions, MNIST, and CIFAR-10. The proposed approach outperforms contrastive-divergence-based methods in every situation considered. The result supports weighted sampling as a useful way to train these models: the sampling procedure and the gradient estimate are designed together, so incomplete exploration does not have to be handled through the same approximations as the standard approach.
neurips-2023-efficient-training-of-energ.tldr: A weighted Langevin sampling method uses the Jarzynski equality to improve energy-based model training and address slow-mixing sampling bias.

paragraphs: Several energy-based learning algorithms are compatible with analog computing, but selecting among them requires comparable evidence. This paper evaluates seven algorithms using the same model family and datasets. They include contrastive learning and variants of equilibrium propagation and coupled learning, which differ in how they perturb a system to obtain contrasting states.

The authors train deep convolutional Hopfield networks on five vision tasks. Although the algorithms perform similarly on MNIST, meaningful differences emerge as tasks become harder. Negative perturbations perform better than positive ones, and centered equilibrium propagation, which uses perturbations of both signs, performs best in the comparison. The paper also supplies theoretical arguments supporting these findings.

The work reports new state-of-the-art results for these Hopfield networks on all five datasets in performance and speed. Its simulations run 13.5 times faster than the referenced earlier implementation, using a new asynchronous energy-minimization algorithm together with 16-bit precision. These speed results concern simulations, while the algorithm comparison informs choices for learning methods compatible with analog hardware.
neurips-2023-energy-based-learning-algor.tldr: A controlled comparison favors centered equilibrium propagation for the tested Hopfield networks and introduces substantially faster simulations.

paragraphs: The paper examines the geometry of CLIP’s image and text representations. The authors observe separate embedding subspaces for the two modalities and analyze representation quality through alignment and uniformity. Their theoretical and empirical analysis finds poor alignment and uniformity even after fine-tuning, which they suggest might restrict transferability and robustness.

Geodesic Multi-Modal Mixup addresses this issue by mixing image and text embeddings on the hypersphere to create hard negative samples. These are challenging examples for contrastive learning to distinguish. Fine-tuning uses the generated negatives together with the original positive and negative examples. The authors support this construction with analysis of its hardness guarantee and limiting behavior.

Experiments span retrieval, calibration, classification under distribution shift, embedding arithmetic, and image captioning. The reported findings show transferable representations that support robust adaptation across these tasks. The approach matters because it turns an observed geometric weakness into a concrete training intervention: changing which difficult examples the model encounters while refining its shared representation space.
neurips-2023-geodesic-multi-modal-mixup-.tldr: Geodesic image-text embedding mixup creates hard negatives that improve representation alignment, uniformity, and adaptation in the reported experiments.

paragraphs: The paper studies compressing a matrix formed by multiplying two narrow matrices and then applying a scalar function separately to each entry. Although the factors have only logarithmic width, the transformed product can be computationally difficult to approximate. Earlier fast relative-error algorithms rely on matching factors and a positive-semidefinite kernel function.

Using reductions from the Strong Exponential Time Hypothesis, the authors establish conditional lower bounds showing why those structural conditions matter for a broad class of functions. In the hard cases, relative-error approximation requires nearly quadratic time, even under some very small rank settings. Polynomial transformations also incur lower bounds involving exponential dependence on the polynomial degree.

The paper complements these barriers with algorithms that match the stated bounds and with a faster additive-error approach based on tensor sketching. This distinguishes two approximation goals whose computational demands can differ substantially. The conditional hardness results also extend to multiplying the transformed matrix by a small matrix, showing that avoiding explicit construction does not automatically avoid the computational obstacle.
neurips-2023-hardness-of-low-rank-approx.tldr: Conditional hardness results identify when entrywise-transformed matrix products resist fast relative-error low-rank approximation, alongside matching algorithms.

paragraphs: Evaluating a causal model involves comparing its predicted effects with effects estimated from an experiment. Randomized controlled trials provide a gold standard, but they are not always feasible or ethical. Conditionally randomized settings offer another route, though inverse probability weighting can introduce substantial variance into the estimated effects and therefore into model assessment.

The paper introduces the pairs estimator to reduce this evaluation noise. Its central idea is to apply the same inverse probability weighting estimator to both the model’s effects and the experimental effects. Using a shared estimation procedure allows weighting-related variation to cancel in the comparison, producing a smaller asymptotic variance for the causal-error estimate.

Empirical studies report improved estimation and suggest the possibility of performance approaching that of randomized controlled trials. That is a potential supported by the experiments, rather than a universal equivalence. The approach is appealing because it changes how model error is evaluated without requiring complicated changes to the underlying inverse probability weighting estimator.
neurips-2023-high-precision-causal-model.tldr: The pairs estimator reduces causal-model evaluation variance by applying the same inverse probability weighting procedure to predicted and experimental effects.

paragraphs: Simulating physical systems can require substantial computation, and learned surrogate models aim to make forecasting cheaper. GraphSplineNets targets the cost within those learned models themselves. Its goal is to reduce both the spatial grid size and the number of iteration steps needed to forecast a system’s evolution.

The method uses two differentiable orthogonal spline collocation techniques to predict responses at arbitrary locations in space and time. This gives the model a way to produce detailed predictions while working with fewer grid points and steps. An adaptive spatial collocation strategy further concentrates sampling on regions judged most important, directing computational effort where it is most useful.

The authors report an improved tradeoff between accuracy and speed across increasingly complex systems: heat dynamics, damped waves, Navier–Stokes equations, and real-world ocean currents. Evaluations include regular and irregular domains. The contribution connects sparse computation with flexible spatial and temporal prediction, showing how surrogate forecasting can become faster without treating a dense grid as the only route to accurate outputs.
neurips-2023-learning-efficient-surrogat.tldr: GraphSplineNets uses differentiable splines and adaptive spatial sampling to improve the accuracy-speed tradeoff of physical-system forecasts.

paragraphs: Off-policy evaluation estimates how a new decision policy would perform using data collected by another policy. Standard estimators can become noisy when the two policies overlap little or when the context and action spaces are large. This paper proposes changing the distributional shift that the estimator focuses on.

The Marginal Ratio estimator works with the shift in the marginal distribution of outcomes, rather than directly focusing on the policies themselves. The authors theoretically analyze its variance advantages over inverse probability weighting and doubly robust estimators. They also connect it to Marginalized Inverse Propensity Score estimation and prove lower variance within a generalized family of those estimators.

Experiments on synthetic and real-world datasets support the theoretical findings. The authors additionally apply the estimator to average treatment effect estimation, reporting improved performance in that causal inference setting. The central contribution is an alternative way to organize reweighting around outcomes, with theoretical and empirical evidence that this can make evaluation more statistically precise.
neurips-2023-marginal-density-ratio-for-.tldr: The Marginal Ratio estimator focuses on outcome-distribution shifts to reduce variance in contextual-bandit policy evaluation.

paragraphs: Offline multi-agent reinforcement learning must learn coordinated behavior from an existing dataset without further interaction with the environment. This is difficult because agents’ decisions are coupled and their joint state-action space is large. Applying data-related regularization separately to each agent can miss constraints that matter for the system as a whole.

OMIGA starts with value regularization at the global level and converts it into equivalent implicit regularizations for individual agents. This provides a principled connection between the team-level learning objective and local learning. The framework also enables in-sample learning, bringing together multi-agent value decomposition, policy learning, and the regularization needed when learning from fixed data.

The authors evaluate OMIGA on offline multi-agent MuJoCo and StarCraft II micromanagement tasks. It outperforms the state-of-the-art offline multi-agent methods in almost all evaluated tasks. These findings support organizing regularization globally while making it usable locally, so that individual policy updates reflect the coupled nature of the overall multi-agent problem.
neurips-2023-offline-multi-agent-reinfor.tldr: OMIGA converts global value regularization into equivalent local regularizations to improve learning from offline multi-agent datasets.

paragraphs: This paper investigates when training a shallow, encoder-only transformer can be shown to converge globally. Its analysis considers finite-width networks and examines architecture, initialization, and scaling together. The main technical obstacle is the softmax operation inside self-attention, whose behavior must be controlled to analyze the network’s training dynamics.

The authors carefully analyze softmax inputs and outputs and distinguish the effects of different scaling schemes. They prove that quadratic overparameterization is sufficient for global convergence of the shallow transformers studied under commonly used He or LeCun initialization. This is a sufficient condition within their setting; it does not establish that quadratic overparameterization is necessary.

A complementary neural tangent kernel analysis allows comparison from another theoretical perspective. Together, the analyses show that scaling and initialization choices play distinct roles in convergence. The contribution is a more architecture-sensitive account of transformer optimization, explaining why details that may appear to be implementation choices can matter to a mathematical understanding of training.
neurips-2023-on-the-convergence-of-encod.tldr: The paper proves sufficient conditions for global convergence of finite-width shallow encoder transformers while distinguishing scaling and initialization effects.

paragraphs: A deployed classifier can assign excessive confidence to unfamiliar inputs. Detecting these out-of-distribution examples is difficult, and existing approaches face tradeoffs: some require expensive training and OOD examples, while many post-hoc methods make limited use of the original training data. OPNP uses that data to guide pruning of an already trained model.

The method first averages gradients over all training samples to assess the sensitivity of parameters and neurons. It then removes those whose sensitivities are exceptionally high or close to zero when making predictions. The aim is to eliminate components associated with overfitting, using information from both extremes of the measured sensitivity distribution.

OPNP requires no additional training and can be combined with other post-hoc methods. Experiments across multiple detection tasks and model architectures report consistently large improvements over the existing methods evaluated. The approach matters because it turns training-data gradients into a practical signal for altering prediction behavior, using the learned model’s internal components to address overconfidence on unfamiliar samples.
neurips-2023-optimal-parameter-and-neuro.tldr: OPNP improves OOD detection by pruning parameters and neurons with extreme training-data gradient sensitivities without additional training.

paragraphs: Markov decision processes support several notions of optimal behavior, including discounted, average, and Blackwell optimality. Solving a discounted problem with a discount factor near one is a common route to average-optimal policies, but existing approaches can depend on strong structural assumptions. The paper identifies difficulties with using the classical Blackwell definition as an algorithmic guide.

The authors introduce a Blackwell discount factor: above this threshold, every discount-optimal policy is also Blackwell-optimal and average-optimal. They derive a general upper bound on the threshold using the bit-size of the process’s rewards and transition probabilities. This supplies a concrete relationship between the numerical description of an instance and a sufficient discount choice.

The result yields a reduction to discounted optimization without the structural assumptions required by earlier approaches, together with new polynomial-time algorithms. The analysis draws on polynomials and algebraic numbers. It also extends to robust Markov decision processes, enabling the first algorithms described in the abstract for computing robust Blackwell-optimal policies.
neurips-2023-reducing-blackwell-and-aver.tldr: A bounded Blackwell discount threshold makes discounted MDP optimization a route to both Blackwell and average optimality without structural assumptions.

paragraphs: Language-model generation stores key and value embeddings from the context in a KV cache. This cache can exceed the memory occupied by model weights and restrict how many requests can be processed together. Scissorhands addresses this growing inference-memory cost by deciding which stored tokens are most worth retaining.

The method builds on a persistence-of-importance hypothesis: tokens that strongly influence one generation step are expected to remain influential later. The authors provide empirical verification and theoretical analysis around this hypothesis. Their system keeps the cache within a fixed memory budget, giving pivotal tokens a higher probability of being stored, without fine-tuning the model.

The reported evaluations achieve up to fivefold reduction in KV-cache memory without compromising model quality. Combining the method with 4-bit quantization yields up to twentyfold compression. These are demonstrated maximum gains rather than guarantees for every workload. The contribution shows how attention-based importance can guide selective memory retention during generation and complement compression through lower numerical precision.
neurips-2023-scissorhands-exploiting-the.tldr: Scissorhands retains likely important tokens within a fixed KV-cache budget, demonstrating up to fivefold memory reduction without model fine-tuning.

paragraphs: A room’s sound depends on its shape, its contents, and where those contents are positioned. Moving a person can therefore change how sound travels through the room. SoundCam provides measurements for studying whether those changes reveal human presence, identity, and position, using room acoustics as a source of information.

The dataset contains 5,000 ten-channel room impulse-response measurements and 2,000 ten-channel music recordings. Collection covers an acoustic laboratory, a living room, and a conference room, with different people positioned throughout each space. Impulse responses characterize the acoustic path between a source and listener, while music recordings offer another way to observe the room’s acoustic properties.

Earlier datasets either lacked systematic object-position variation or relied entirely on simulation. SoundCam addresses that gap with real measurements and varied human locations. The authors describe it as the largest publicly released collection of unique impulse responses from in-the-wild rooms at the time, and demonstrate uses including human detection, identification, and position tracking.
neurips-2023-soundcam-a-dataset-for-find.tldr: SoundCam records how people change room acoustics and demonstrates that these measurements can support detection, identification, and tracking.

paragraphs: SPAE addresses how a language model with fixed parameters can work with visual content. Its approach converts between raw pixels and interpretable words drawn from the language model’s existing vocabulary. This creates a representation that the model can process through language while retaining information needed to reconstruct visual outputs.

The resulting tokens capture both semantic content and fine visual detail. Those two requirements matter together: a representation must convey what an image means for understanding tasks, while preserving enough detail for generation. SPAE therefore serves as a conversion mechanism connecting visual inputs and outputs with the vocabulary of a frozen language model.

The authors validate the approach through in-context learning experiments with frozen PaLM 2 and GPT 3.5 on image understanding and generation tasks. They report the first successful image-content generation by a frozen LLM and more than 25% improvement over state-of-the-art image-understanding performance under the same setting. These findings support multimodal capabilities through representation conversion without changing the language model’s parameters.
neurips-2023-spae-semantic-pyramid-autoe.tldr: SPAE translates visual content into vocabulary tokens so frozen language models can perform image understanding and generation.

paragraphs: Group distributionally robust optimization seeks a model that performs well across multiple distributions. The paper formulates this as a stochastic convex-concave saddle-point problem. Stochastic mirror descent reaches an epsilon-optimal solution with sample complexity proportional to m log(m)/epsilon squared, matching the stated lower bound up to a logarithmic factor.

An online-learning formulation then reduces sampling from one example per distribution each round to a single example per round while preserving total sample complexity. It treats optimization as a two-player game combining mirror descent with a non-oblivious multi-armed bandit algorithm. This changes the sampling workload of individual rounds without worsening the overall theoretical sample requirement.

The authors also study unequal sample budgets through weighted objectives. One approach respects budgets in expectation through nonuniform sampling. Another uses minibatches to meet budgets exactly and reduce gradient variance, then applies stochastic mirror-prox. Under appropriate conditions, the latter achieves distribution-specific convergence rates within a logarithmic factor of the optimal rate for learning each distribution separately.
neurips-2023-stochastic-approximation-ap.tldr: The paper develops sample-efficient group-robust optimization algorithms, including methods that accommodate unequal sampling budgets across distributions.

paragraphs: Optimal transport matches two collections of mass, but conventional solvers face both computational and modeling difficulties. Standard sample-based methods can cost cubic time in the number of samples. Requiring all mass to be matched can also make the result sensitive to outliers, because every point must participate in the matching.

Two research directions address these issues separately. Low-rank solvers offer the prospect of linear-time computation, while unbalanced transport relaxes exact mass conservation through penalties. This paper brings the two ideas together, aiming for solvers that combine scalable representations with flexibility about how much mass is matched.

The authors develop custom algorithms for both the linear optimal transport problem and its Fused-Gromov-Wasserstein generalization. They demonstrate practical relevance on challenging spatial transcriptomics matching problems. The contribution is the integration of two complementary improvements: reducing the cost of representing and computing a match while easing the requirement to force every part of both inputs into that match.
neurips-2023-unbalanced-low-rank-optimal.tldr: New transport algorithms combine low-rank computation with relaxed mass conservation and demonstrate usefulness for spatial transcriptomics matching.

paragraphs: Graph neural networks use varied pretraining strategies, which makes it difficult to design a prompting method that applies broadly. Existing specialized approaches can depend on a particular pretraining task, such as edge prediction. Graph Prompt Feature, or GPF, addresses this fragmentation by applying prompts in the input graph’s feature space.

The authors theoretically show that GPF can achieve an effect equivalent to any form of prompting function. This avoids explicitly designing a separate prompting function for each pretraining strategy. Instead, the method adaptively obtains a prompted graph for the downstream task. The paper provides derivations supporting both its universality and effectiveness.

Experiments across different pretraining strategies report average improvements over fine-tuning of about 1.4% with full-shot data and 3.2% with few-shot data. GPF also substantially outperforms specialized prompting methods on models using their intended pretraining strategies. These results support a common feature-space mechanism as a useful alternative to adapting each pretrained graph model through a separately designed prompt.
neurips-2023-universal-prompt-tuning-for.tldr: GPF prompts graph input features to provide a theoretically universal adaptation method with reported gains over fine-tuning and specialized prompts.
